oauthclients.title: ChatGPT connector
oauthclients.intro: OAuth clients for native “Sign in” integrations (e.g. a ChatGPT custom GPT). On authorization the client gets operator access (all instances). The client secret is shown ONCE.
oauthclients.name: Name
oauthclients.redirectsHint: The client’s allowed return addresses, one per line. ChatGPT shows it when you set up the action (form: https://chat.openai.com/aip/…/oauth/callback).
oauthclients.redirectsOptional: You can leave this empty for now and add it later — ChatGPT only shows the callback URL AFTER you save the action.
oauthclients.created: Connector created. Copy the client secret now — it will not be shown again.
oauthclients.consentIntro: “{0}” wants access to your MatCMS Cloud.
oauthclients.warn: Warning: this grants the application FULL operator access to ALL your instances — including pulling and uploading backups and live restore. Only allow it if you started this yourself. You can revoke the access any time under “API keys”.
oauthclients.secretOnce: The client secret is shown only when created. Lost it? Just create a new connector.
oauthclients.setupHeading: How to connect ChatGPT – step by step
oauthclients.setupStep1: In ChatGPT, edit the GPT → “Actions” → “Authentication” → choose “OAuth”.
oauthclients.setupStep2: Enter the values below: Client ID, Client secret, Authorization URL, Token URL and Scope. Token exchange method: POST (default).
oauthclients.setupStep3: Save in ChatGPT. ChatGPT now shows you a callback URL.
oauthclients.setupStep4: Add that callback URL here on the connector via “Edit”, under “Redirect URIs”, and save.
oauthclients.setupStep5: Done. Click “Sign in” in the GPT → “Allow access” in the browser. No extra software needed.
settings.aiProviderHint: More providers to come; the model is set centrally.
edgeguard.title: Access guard: only through the edge
edgeguard.intro: Closes this node's automatic addresses to everybody but this cloud's edge proxy: the node's proxy only answers requests that carry a secret key in a header, which only the edge knows and sends. Customer domains that run at the edge keep working; this node's own addresses are no longer reachable from outside (403).
edgeguard.onConfirm: Open this node's automatic addresses only for the edge? Direct requests without the key get 403 afterwards.
edgeguard.rotateConfirm: Renew the key? The websites of this node are unreachable for a few seconds meanwhile.
edgeguard.offConfirm: Switch the guard off? This node's addresses are directly reachable again afterwards.
edgeguard.issues: Not everything was applied as asked:
edgeguard.hint: Requirements: edge proxy switched on, a proxy on the node that can do it (Caddy or Matcad 0.9 and later), automatic addresses on the node, an up-to-date agent and a reachable node. The key is stored encrypted and never shown. Important: the guard covers the addresses at the node's proxy. The published container ports (the node's port range) are independent of it – open them to the edge only, with a firewall. Instances without a customer domain at the edge are closed to everybody afterwards.

settings.aiModelChatGptHint: With the ChatGPT sign-in only models the account offers count – the suggestion list comes from ChatGPT.
settings.chatgptIntro: Instead of an API key the cloud can use a ChatGPT account, like Codex and Hermes: the cloud shows a code, you type it on the ChatGPT page, and the cloud is signed in. This is an unofficial route that OpenAI can change at any time. All approved websites then share this one account and its quota.
settings.chatgptWaiting: Waiting for the confirmation at ChatGPT …
settings.chatgptExpired: The code has expired. Please sign in again.
settings.chatgptNotActive: Signed in, but not yet chosen as the provider: pick "ChatGPT sign-in" above, enter a model and save.
settings.chatgptLogoutConfirm: Sign the cloud out of ChatGPT? The AI features of all websites stay silent until a provider is set up.

profiles.aiInstructionPlaceholder: e.g. Vacation rental on the Baltic coast. Tone: warm, inviting. Language: German. Always mention the sea view and the quiet location.
profiles.aiInstructionHint: Comes before every use of AI on assigned instances – AI assistant, chat bot, plugins, theme, meta, teaser. After it comes "About this website", which each instance keeps itself (Settings → AI).
profiles.aiBudgetHint: The cloud grants and enforces it; the instance never sees the number. Over budget, AI features pause until the month rolls over.
profiles.aiBackupBeforeHint: The site takes a local restore point before every AI content change (via MCP), so an unwanted change can be rolled back.
profiles.aiGuidesHint: Extra guidance per AI action — prepended to that action's built-in prompt (augments, does not replace it). Empty = only the good defaults.

profiles.aiGuideSitePlaceholder: e.g. Always create Home, About, Offer and Contact pages. Short, clear copy, no jargon.
profiles.aiGuideThemePlaceholder: e.g. Calm, light colors; high contrast for readability; rounded buttons.
profiles.aiGuideSeoPlaceholder: e.g. Concise, under 155 characters, with a clear call to action; mention the brand at the end.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.intro: A profile bundles configuration and rules. Instances that enroll with a profile's join code land in it automatically and receive its settings.
profiles.createIntro: Name and description are enough. Join code, contents and behaviour are set on the profile itself afterwards.
profiles.deleteConfirm: Really delete this profile? Assigned instances keep running but stop receiving configuration.
profiles.rotateConfirm: Issue a new join code? The old one stops working. Already connected instances are unaffected.
profiles.autoApproveHint: Off: an instance enrolling with this code waits for your approval and receives no configuration until then.
profiles.revisionHint: bumped on every change; instances pull the new configuration when it moves
profiles.payloadsHint: What this profile rolls out to its instances.
profiles.strategyHint: Per area: how far the profile reaches into the instance.
profiles.mode.keep.hint: The instance is brought in line with the profile on every change — local changes are overwritten.
profiles.mode.add.hint: Only what is missing on the instance gets added. Anything already there stays as it is.
profiles.mode.once.hint: Rolled out in full once and never touched again — not even when the profile changes later.
profiles.usersAddOnly: Users are always add-only — existing accounts on the instance are never changed or deleted.
profiles.removeDefaultAdmin.hint: Removes the built-in admin/admin login — but only if it still has the default password AND another admin exists. This can never lock anyone out. Ideal for shedding the default login after rolling out your own admin.
profiles.smtpHint: These SMTP details are written into the settings of every assigned instance.
profiles.smtpEnableHint: Off: instances keep their own mail configuration. The values stored here are kept, they are just not sent.
profiles.otherSettingsHint: Any MatCMS setting key as a key/value pair.
profiles.usersHint: These accounts are created on the instances if they do not exist there yet. The password is hashed once here; the cloud never stores the plaintext.
profiles.pluginsHint: Plugin packages as produced by MatCMS under Plugins, Export. Same key = update on the instance.
profiles.pluginUploadHint: Passed through unchanged to the instances, which apply it via their own import.
profiles.componentsHint: Reusable blocks. The type is the identity — an existing type is updated on the instance.
profiles.componentFieldsHint: Same format as the MatCMS component editor, e.g. [{"id":"title","label":"Title","type":"text"}]
profiles.previewNote: Preview only — clicks have no effect.
profiles.dbgOk: All placeholders map to a field.
profiles.templatePreviewHint: Sample page rendered with the values in this form
profiles.previewHeroText: A paragraph of body text, to judge font, line height and text colour.
profiles.pluginEditHint: The package is repacked on save — instances still receive exactly the ZIP their own importer expects. Bundled files are preserved untouched.
profiles.pluginCodeHint: Runs server-side on the instance. After rollout the plugin stays disabled there until somebody enables it.
profiles.pluginVersionHint: Raise it so instances pick the new build up — an unchanged version is skipped.
profiles.pluginFilesHint: Part of the plugin, loaded from the entry file with #load. Preserved unchanged when you save — they are edited in the instance's own plugin editor.
profiles.pluginDeleteConfirm: Remove this plugin from the profile? It stays on the instances.
profiles.addFromStoreHint: Entries from the global store. They are taken by reference — change the entry in the store and every profile that took it gets the new version.
profiles.storeEmpty: There is nothing (left) in the store this profile could take.
profiles.useGlobalSmtp: Roll out the global SMTP settings
profiles.useGlobalSmtpHint: Takes the SMTP configuration from Settings, SMTP. The profile's own settings still override individual keys.
profiles.userPasswordHint: When editing, leaving this empty keeps the current password.
profiles.userDeleteConfirm: Remove this user from the profile? Accounts already rolled out stay on the instances.
profiles.settingKeyHint: A MatCMS setting key, e.g. site.canonicalUrl or analytics.ga4.
profiles.settingDeleteConfirm: Remove this setting from the profile? The value stays on the instances.
profiles.noUsers: No users in this profile yet.
profiles.noPlugins: No plugins in this profile yet.
profiles.noComponents: No components in this profile yet.
profiles.noTemplates: No templates in this profile yet.
profiles.componentTypeHint: Lowercase, hyphenated. This is the identity on the instance and should not change afterwards.
profiles.templateNameHint: This is the identity on the instance — a template of the same name is updated there.
tplfiles.intro: The layout files of this template. Each is optional — if empty, the built-in default behavior applies; if filled, it is loaded/included. Click to edit.
tplfiles.insertDefaultConfirm: The default replaces the content of this file. Continue?
tplfiles.pick: Pick a file in the tree
tplfiles.body.desc: Overall layout of the <body>. Only takes effect if it contains {{content}} — otherwise the default layout stays active. Menus via {{menu:slot}}.
tplfiles.article.desc: Layout of a single blog detail page (/blog/…). Without customization the built-in layout is used.
tplfiles.styles.desc: Additional CSS. Included as <style> on every page when present.
tplfiles.script.desc: Additional JavaScript. Included before </body> on every page when present.
tplfiles.maintenance.desc: Maintenance page (complete HTML document). Shown while maintenance mode is active.

profiles.tplParametersHint: JSON array [{ id, label, type, options, default }]. Types: text|select|color|number|bool. Referenced in CSS/layout as {{param:id}}.
profiles.tplMenuMapHint: An object { "slot": "menuKey" }. Resolves {{menu:slot}} in the layout against the instance's menus.
profiles.componentDeleteConfirm: Remove this component from the profile? It stays on the instances.
profiles.templatesHint: Designs rolled out to every assigned instance. The name is the identity. The quickest route is to build the template in MatCMS and import its JSON here.
profiles.templateDeleteConfirm: Remove this template from the profile? It stays on the instances.
profiles.templateImportHint: Paste the JSON from MatCMS under Templates, open a template, "Export as JSON". A template of the same name is overwritten.
profiles.activateTemplateHint: Leaving this empty means templates are rolled out but the instance decides which one is live. Switching the design of a running customer site should be a deliberate act.
profiles.tplLayoutHint: Only applied when it contains {{content}} — otherwise the default layout is used. The document head stays managed either way.
profiles.tplPartsHint: An object like { "post": "<html …>" }. Page types not listed use the built-in layout.

enroll.displayNameHint: A free display name. If set, it is kept and NOT replaced by the name the instance reports. Empty = take the instance's own name.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.updateAgentConfirm: Update the agent now? The node is disconnected for about a minute; its sites keep running.
nodes.commandTitle: Start the agent on the host
nodes.commandOnce: Run this command on the host. The token is shown in plain text only now — it is stored as a hash. If it is lost: “Issue new token”.
nodes.runCommandHint: Run on the host. Replace <TOKEN> with the agent's token — it is stored only as a hash and cannot be shown again. “New token” shows the complete command once.
nodes.composeHint: For a host without a proxy of its own that should serve sites itself over HTTPS. Save as docker-compose.node.yaml and start with docker compose -f docker-compose.node.yaml up -d (80/443 must be free). Still open: <MATCAD-KEY>: a long random value, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32 — the same value then goes into this node's Proxy tab as the key. If a Caddy already runs on the host, use the compose above instead and set this node's proxy to “Caddy” (admin URL).
nodes.composeAgentHint: The same as the start command, as a compose file. Without a proxy on the node the edge reaches the sites at node address:port (the node's port range, over HTTP) — firewall: open those ports for the edge only. Save as docker-compose.node-agent.yaml and start with docker compose -f docker-compose.node-agent.yaml up -d.
nodes.rotateConfirm: Issue a new token? The running agent is turned away at once until it is restarted with the new command.
nodes.revokeConfirm: Revoke this node? It receives no more jobs; its sites keep running.
nodes.deleteConfirm: Delete this node? Its sites keep running, but the cloud can no longer act on them.
nodes.portsHint: Every new instance on this node gets its host port from this range. The node itself decides which one is free.
nodes.proxyHint: The proxy is reached from the node, not from the cloud — so enter addresses as the node sees them. The test runs on the node too.
nodes.whereHint: This host or a connected node. The domain is published on the same host.
migrate.title: Move
migrate.notManaged: Moving is only possible for instances this cloud created itself — the old container is retired or removed in the process.
migrate.confirm: Move the site now? It is offline during the move (a few minutes, depending on its size).
migrate.hint: The data moves 1:1 — content, uploads, users and the cloud link stay as they are. The domain moves along; its DNS record must then point at the new host. If anything fails, the site runs at its old place again.
migrate.removeSource: Remove the old copy afterwards (container and volume)
migrate.removeSourceHint: Unticked, the old copy is only retired: stopped, renamed, never starts by itself again — the way back stays open.
cloudupdate.title: This cloud
cloudupdate.confirm: Update the cloud now? It will be unreachable for 1–2 minutes. If the new version does not come up, it rolls back automatically (including the database).
cloudupdate.help: A short-lived helper container pulls the new image, swaps the cloud container, health-checks it and rolls back on failure.

cleanup.noAnalysis: No analysis for this instance yet.
cleanup.mediaHelp: Images whose file name appears nowhere in the instance's content (conservative). Note: some may be images the owner simply hasn't placed yet.
cleanup.componentsHelp: Components with no placed block. Note: components rolled out via profile/store come back on the next sync — remove them there.
cleanup.pluginsHelp: No automatic "unused" detection (they run server-side). Tick deliberately; nothing is preselected.

logs.noneInstance: No errors reported by this instance – or it does not send them yet (older version).
logs.cfg.requests.help: In addition to errors, record every HTTP request to the cloud (category “Requests”). Static files are skipped. Can create many entries – cap the retention below.
logs.cfg.retention.help: Older entries are deleted hourly. 0 = do not delete by age (only the hard cap applies).
logs.fullPending: Full log requested – will be uploaded on the instance's next contact.
apikeys.title: API keys
apikeys.intro: Keys for the programmatic interface (/api/v1): pull an instance's backup, upload an edited one and — with an extra right — restore it live. A key is shown only once, when it is created.
apikeys.name: Name
apikeys.nameHint: For your own overview only — what or who the key is for.
apikeys.canRestoreHint: Without this, the key can only pull and upload backups. Restoring overwrites the LIVE site and must be granted on purpose.
apikeys.canManageProfilesHint: Allows creating and editing profiles and their payloads (settings, users, plugins, components, templates) and assigning instances via the API. A profile change affects every assigned instance.
apikeys.canManageHostingHint: Allows via the API: start/stop/restart/update instance containers and read their logs (within the key's instance scope). With "All instances" additionally: switch the Hosting module and update the cloud itself.
apikeys.canManageStoreHint: Allows creating, editing and removing the cloud-wide catalogue entries (templates, plugins, components, mail templates) via the API. A store entry is shared by every profile that selects it — a change reaches all of those profiles and their instances.
apikeys.revokeConfirm: Revoke this key? It will stop working afterwards.
apikeys.newOnce: Copy it now — the key is shown this one time only and cannot be retrieved afterwards.

instances.title: Instances
instances.empty: No instance connected yet. Create one and paste its id and token into MatCMS.
instances.outdatedProtocolHint: The instance speaks an older protocol version than this cloud.
instances.pendingHint: Id and token have not been entered in MatCMS yet.
instances.stopConfirm: Stop the instance container? The site will be offline until it is started again.
instances.restartConfirm: Restart the instance container? The site is briefly unreachable during the restart.
instances.remoteHint: runs on a different Docker host, updates are notify-only
instances.nameHint: Just a label for this overview. The instance reports its own site name on the first heartbeat.
instances.tokenOnce: The token is shown this one time only. Just its hash is stored.
instances.pairingHint: Enter these three values in MatCMS under Settings, Cloud. The instance then checks in by itself.
instances.updateConfirm: Really recreate the container from the new image? The site is briefly unavailable.
instances.updateRemote: This instance does not run on this Docker host. Run the update there:
instances.rotateConfirm: Issue a new token? The instance loses the connection until the new token is entered there.
instances.deleteConfirm: Really remove this instance? Its history is deleted with it.
instances.removeOwnHint: This cloud created the container, so it may also take it down again.
instances.removeForeignHint: This instance merely connected — its container is not managed by this cloud. It can be unregistered here; its container and its data are left alone.
instances.removeBackupsValue: {0} — they go with the instance, whichever way is chosen.
instances.removeUnregisterHint: The site keeps running unchanged. Only the cloud link and the history here go away.
instances.removeKeepData: Remove the container, keep the volumes
instances.removeKeepDataHint: The site is stopped and its container removed. The data stays on its volume.
instances.removeFullHint: Container and volumes are deleted. Everything on this site is gone for good afterwards.
instances.removeConfirmFull: Remove “{0}” completely? Container AND volumes are deleted. Everything on this site is gone for good afterwards.
instances.uploadBackupHint: A MatCMS backup ZIP from your own machine. It is stored as one of this instance's backups; “restore immediately” plays it back on the instance's next contact. The instance keeps its cloud link across the restore.
instances.backupRequestHint: The cloud asks the instance for a backup on its next heartbeat; the instance makes it itself and uploads it. It counts as arrived only once the file is here — not when the instance reported it.
instances.removeBackupFirst: Fetch a backup, then remove completely
instances.removeBackupFirstHint: In that order: the cloud asks the instance for a backup, waits until it has actually arrived here, and only then removes container and volumes. If no backup arrives, NOTHING is removed — the operation stays visibly on hold until the backup is here or you take it back.
instances.removeBackupFirstArchive: This one backup outlives the removal: it is moved to the archive before anything is deleted, and can be found afterwards under Backups → Archive. The instance's other backups go with it, as they do on every other way.
instances.removeBackupFirstOutdated: “Fetch a backup, then remove completely” is not available here: this instance still speaks an older version of the protocol and cannot answer a backup request. The way appears once the instance has been updated.
instances.removeConfirmBackupFirst: Ask “{0}” for a backup and remove the instance completely afterwards? Nothing is removed until the backup has really arrived in the cloud.
instances.removeWaiting: Removal on hold — waiting for the backup
instances.removeWaitingNoDeadline: There is no deadline: nothing is removed “to be safe” once some waiting period has passed. The operation ends only by the backup arriving — or by you taking it back here. If it waits too long, the cloud sends an e-mail.
instances.removePendingHint: A removal is on hold for this instance. It happens only once the requested backup has arrived in the cloud.
settings.title: Settings
settings.canonicalUrlHint: You sign in here and new instances enrol here; links in e-mails point here. Not to be confused with the domain for instance addresses (Hosting → Hosts → Proxy).
settings.recipientsHint: Comma separated. Empty = every user of this cloud that has an e-mail address.

settings.autoUpdateLocalHint: Applies to instances on this host and on nodes. On failure the old container is rolled back.
settings.smtpSsl: Force SSL/TLS (port 465 always uses implicit SSL)

users.roleHelp: An administrator sees and manages the whole cloud. An operator only sees and operates the instances selected below — no profiles, store, users, settings or API keys.
users.instancesHelp: The operator may only see and operate these instances (backup, restore, update). No selection = no access.
users.noInstances: There are no instances to assign yet.

import.userHint: JSON with username, e-mail and password hash. The plaintext password is stored nowhere and is therefore not part of the import.

add.smtpSource: Where do the values come from?
add.smtpGlobalHint: Use the cloud’s SMTP configuration — changes there then apply here too.
add.smtpOwnHint: For this profile only, independent of the global configuration.
profiles.smtpRemoveConfirm: Stop rolling SMTP out? The values are kept, and instances keep the configuration they have.
profiles.mailSource: How do the instances send mail?
profiles.mailViaCloudHint: The instances do not send at all — every message goes to the cloud, which spools it and delivers it with its own sender address. No SMTP credentials on the instances.
spool.title: Spooler
spool.none: This instance has not handed over a message yet.
spool.subject: Subject
spool.hint: Messages from this instance sent through the cloud. A failed delivery is retried with a growing delay; after eight attempts it counts as given up and can be put back in the queue by hand here.
profiles.noMailTemplates: This profile does not roll out any mail templates yet.
store.noMailTemplates: No mail templates in the store yet.
mailtpl.title: Mail template
mailtpl.keyHint: Names WHICH mail this is — e.g. form.submission. The instance matches on it; a key it does not know is stored and never used.
mailtpl.subject: Subject
mailtpl.bodyHint: Placeholders in double braces, e.g. {{form_name}}. Which ones exist depends on the mail and is listed in the instance editor.
mailtpl.enabledHint: Off means the instance does not send this mail. The template is kept.
mailtpl.importHint: Paste the JSON from a mail template editor. A template with the same key is overwritten.
mailtpl.deleteConfirm: Remove the template from the store? Profiles lose the selection; instances keep the text.
mailtpl.removeConfirm: Remove the template from the profile? Instances keep the text.
mailtpl.isHtmlHint: The body is then HTML. The instance still sends both — an HTML-only message scores worse with spam filters, so the text version is derived from it.
spool.noneAtAll: No instance has handed over a message yet.
spool.clearConfirm: Remove all delivered and given-up messages? Waiting ones are kept.
mailtpl.unknownKeyCloud: This cloud knows no mail with that key — the wording can still be written and rolled out, there are just no documented placeholders here:
mailtpl.loopsHint: Everything between {{#name}} and {{/name}} is written once per entry — the same notation the template engine uses for menus.
mailtpl.placeholdersHint: Clicking inserts the placeholder at the cursor — in the subject or the body, whichever you were in last.
mailtpl.previewHint: Shows the body with example values, rendered by the same code that sends the mail — loops run twice, so it is visible what repetition does to the layout.
profiles.translationRemoveConfirm: Stop rolling out the translation credentials? The values are kept, and instances keep what they have.
profiles.translateProviderHint: Leaving it empty switches machine translation off on the instances.
profiles.translateUrlHint: LibreTranslate only: the reachable address of your own instance.
profiles.translateApiKeyHint: Stored encrypted. Leave empty to keep the stored key.
add.translationHint: Give the instances credentials for machine translation.
backups.title: Backups
backups.none: No instance has uploaded a backup yet.
backups.restoreConfirm: Restore this backup onto the instance? The site’s current state is overwritten. The instance carries it out on its next contact.
backups.deleteConfirm: Delete the backup? The instance keeps its own copy, if it still has one.
backups.orphansHint: What does not add up between disk and database. A FILE with no row is what deleting an instance leaves behind — the rows go with it, the bytes do not. A ROW with no file is what clearing out the volume by hand leaves behind. Neither is dangerous, and neither can be restored.
backups.cleanConfirm: Remove all orphaned files and rows?
settings.backupQuotaHint: Beyond it, that instance’s oldest backup is dropped. Leave empty for the default.
profiles.backupInactiveHint: Not rolled out yet. Saving makes this profile own the backup settings and send them to its instances.
profiles.backupRetainHint: How many backups stay on the instance
profiles.backupContentHint: Always the whole section — picking single pages or forms would come up empty on every other instance.
profiles.backupToCloud: Hand finished backups to the cloud
profiles.backupToCloudHint: From there they can be downloaded and restored.
profiles.backupRemoveConfirm: Stop rolling out the backup settings? Nothing changes on the instances.
add.backupHint: Schedule, contents and whether backups land in the cloud
profiles.backupQuotaHint: Per instance of this profile. Empty = the default profile's quota ({0} GB). When an instance is full, its oldest backup goes at the next upload.
backups.archiveHint: Backups whose instance was removed. They were secured before the removal and belong to no instance any more — so no quota applies here and nothing is cleaned up automatically. In use: {0}.
backups.archiveNone: There is nothing in the archive.
backups.archiveDeleteConfirm: Delete this archived backup for good? Its instance no longer exists — this is the last copy.
instances.previewInsecure: This site is served over http and cannot be embedded in an https page — the browser blocks it. Usually the instance sits behind a proxy and reports its own address as http; forwarded headers or a canonical URL in the site settings fix that.
settings.forceHttpsHint: For instances behind a TLS-terminating proxy: they report http although they are reachable over https, and an https admin may then neither frame nor link them. Only switch this on if every instance really is on https.
settings.hostingEnabledHint: Lets the cloud create new MatCMS instances — on this host and on nodes. Off hides Nodes, Domains and “New instance”.
settings.hostingProxyNone: No proxy (instances directly on their port)
settings.hostingProxyHint: Without a proxy every instance is reached on its host port; a domain is then only recorded. With Matcad or Caddy the cloud creates the route including its TLS certificate when publishing, and removes it again.
settings.hostingMatcadUrlHint: The base address the cloud reaches the Matcad API at (without /api/v1). The access key is Matcad’s API key.
settings.hostingCaddyServerHint: Name of the HTTP server in Caddy’s configuration the routes go into (default srv0). It must listen on :443 for Caddy to obtain certificates automatically. Other routes there are left untouched.
settings.hostingUpstream: How does the proxy reach the instance?
settings.hostingUpstreamHint: Network: when publishing, the cloud attaches the container to the proxy’s network, which then reaches it by name. Host port: the proxy goes to the published port via the given host address.
settings.hostingProxyUpstreamHost: Host address as seen by the proxy
settings.hostingPortsHint: Each new instance gets its host port from this range — behind a proxy too.
settings.hostingPortsUsed: ({0} ports in use on the host)
instances.newNameHint: Container and volume name are derived from this.
instances.newProfileHint: The new site enrols itself with this profile's join code, and starts with whatever the profile rolls out.
instances.newVersionHint: Image tag, e.g. latest. Latest published:
instances.newDomainMatcad: Optional — the route including its certificate is created right away. Empty: reachable on the host port, domain later in the Hosting tab.
instances.newDomainPlain: Optional — without a proxy it is only recorded. The instance is reachable on its host port.
settings.hostingNamePatternHint: {name} is replaced by the site name, lowercased and hyphenated the way Docker does it. The name is used for stack, container and volume.
add.whichInstance: How should the instance be added?
add.instanceNewHint: The cloud creates a new site and starts it.
add.instanceAdoptHint: The cloud enrols itself at a running site.
add.instanceJoinHint: The site enrols itself with the cloud.
add.instanceNewOff: Switch hosting on first — this way.
profiles.componentIconHelp: Shown next to the component in the instance block editor.
profiles.componentFieldsHelp: Every field is asked for in the instance block editor. The label becomes the {{field}} placeholder for the template; renaming keeps the old placeholder so blocks already placed keep working.
updates.title: Update instances
updates.none: No instance with an available update that the cloud can update itself.
docker.pruneNone: No old MatCMS images to clean up.
updates.cloudBusy: The cloud is updating itself right now — start again afterwards.
cloudupdate.screen.title: The cloud is being updated
cloudupdate.screen.wait: Please wait. The cloud will be unreachable for a minute or two; this page reloads by itself afterwards.
cloudupdate.screen.current: The cloud is up to date.
cloudupdate.screen.rolledBack: The new version did not come up — the cloud runs the previous version again.
docker.noImages: No MatCMS images on this host.
nodes.step1: Give it a name here and create the node.
nodes.step2: The cloud then shows a docker run command once. Run it on the new server — it only needs Docker; no open port, just outbound access to this cloud.
nodes.step3: The agent reports within seconds and the node shows as online. In the node's “Proxy & ports” tab, set how its sites are reached — then “New instance” can create sites on it.
autodomain.title: Automatic addresses
autodomain.enable: Every instance gets an address automatically
autodomain.baseHint: Every instance gets <name>.<this domain>. Set a wildcard DNS record *.<this domain> to this server.
matcad.settingsHint: The address Let's Encrypt notifies about expiring certificates, and the DNS waits for wildcard certificates.
matcad.routeDeleteConfirm: Delete domain "{0}" in Matcad? It will no longer be reachable.
matcad.noRoutes: Matcad does not serve any domain yet.
matcad.upstreamHint: Container name and port on the proxy's network, e.g. http://matcms-cloud:8080 – or host:port.
matcad.wildcard: Wildcard (*.domain, one certificate for all subdomains)
matcad.wildcardHint: A wildcard certificate needs the DNS challenge – Matcad needs a DNS provider for it.
matcad.providersHint: Access to your domain registrar's DNS API. Matcad needs it for wildcard certificates (DNS challenge).
matcad.providerSecretHint: Secret fields are never shown again; leaving one empty keeps the stored value.
cfgbackup.createHint: Backs up the settings of THIS cloud – not the websites (they have their own backups). To move: download here, upload on the new cloud and restore.
cfgbackup.section.profiles: Profiles (with settings, users, plugins, components, templates)
cfgbackup.section.hosting: Server/hosting (address, proxy, Matcad, ports, automatic addresses)
cfgbackup.passphraseHint: Secrets (SMTP password, AI key, proxy keys, 2FA) are only included with a password and are encrypted with it – keep it safe, without it they are lost. At least 8 characters.
cfgbackup.uploadHint: A downloaded backup, e.g. from the old cloud. It then appears in the list.
cfgbackup.restoreHint: Run "Preview" first – it shows what would change and changes nothing. Settings of the chosen sections are overwritten, profiles replaced or created by name, store items updated or created. Users are only added – a restore never changes an existing account.
cfgbackup.hostingWarn: belongs to the backup's server, only choose it for the same server
cfgbackup.restorePassHint: The password the backup was created with. Empty = secrets stay as they are here.
cfgbackup.applyConfirm: Restore the chosen sections now? Settings and profiles of this cloud are overwritten.
extradomain.title: Further domains
extradomain.addWww: Also create the www variant (redirect to the domain)
extradomain.hint: For www.… and old domains. They live where the main domain lives and follow it on a change or a move. Each must point to this server in DNS. "Redirect" is the usual choice – search engines then see a single address.
extradomain.removeConfirm: Remove "{0}"? The address will no longer be reachable.
autodomain.sameAsCloud: Same name as the cloud's address – that is fine: the cloud sits on the domain itself, the instances below it.
matcad.baseDomainFollows: follows the domain for instance addresses (Proxy tab)
addr.title: Addresses of this server
addr.name: Name
addr.cloudMissing: {0} does not resolve – set an A record (or CNAME) to this server.
addr.cloudUnset: Set Settings → General → Address of this cloud; without it new instances cannot enrol.
addr.wildcardMissing: DNS is missing {0} → {1}. Without it the instance addresses are unreachable. Watch for typos in the host field.
addr.wildcardElsewhere: {0} does not point to the same server as the cloud ({1}).
addr.certificateNone: No wildcard certificate – every instance address gets its own.
addr.hint: Names are resolved freshly on every visit. "DNS now" shows what the world sees right now – after a change at the DNS provider it can take a few minutes.
edge.whatTitle: What is the edge proxy for?
edge.what: Only useful with several servers: all customer domains then point to ONE address (the edge) and the cloud forwards internally to the site's server. When a site moves servers, only the forwarding changes, not DNS. With a single server it adds nothing – leave it off.
edge.sketch:
Without edge:  customer-a.com → IP server 1      customer-b.com → IP server 2
With edge:     customer-a.com ┐
               customer-b.com ┴→ IP edge → forwarded to server 1 or 2
matcad.propagationHint: Wildcard certificates only: how long Caddy waits for the DNS record to be visible for the check. 0 = default. netcup is slow – use delay 600 and timeout 1200 there, or the certificate fails.
wildcard.providerMatcadHint: The DNS provider that hosts the domain. It is stored in Matcad and its credentials stay there – edit them on the "Matcad" tab.
wildcard.netcupHint: In the netcup Customer Control Panel (CCP) under Master Data → API: customer number, API key and API password. Then set the DNS delay to 600 seconds on the "Matcad" tab – netcup takes that long to make a record visible.
edge.title: Edge proxy for customer domains
edge.enable: Route customer domains through this cloud's edge proxy
edge.enableHint: Customer domains then point at the cloud server; the edge forwards to the instance's host. A move only changes the target — no DNS change.
edge.useHostProxy: Use the same proxy as “This host”
edge.matcadNote: Matcad can only rewrite the Host header from version 0.9. An older Matcad as the edge only forwards to node-address:port (set an address per node). With Caddy or Matcad 0.9 and later it goes through the automatic addresses – and only then is a node's access guard ("only through the edge") possible.
edge.moveConfirm: Move the existing customer domains now? Their old routes are removed — the domains' DNS must point at the new entry.
edge.nodeAddressHint: IP or host name under which the edge reaches this node (public or private network). Only needed when the edge forwards to address:port.
hosting.hostAddressRemoveConfirm: Remove the host address? The instance is then no longer reachable under it.
hosting.publishHintEdge: Published at this cloud's edge proxy — the domain's DNS must point at the cloud server.
profiles.backupQuotaHintDefault: Per instance. This default profile is the fallback for every other profile and for instances without one. Empty = {0} GB.
profiles.recommendedMissing: {0} recommended setting(s) missing in this profile:
wildcard.enable: One wildcard certificate for all addresses (DNS challenge)
wildcard.providerHint: Caddy: the DNS module, e.g. hetzner, cloudflare or netcup — it must be built into this Caddy. Matcad: the name of the DNS provider as set up in Matcad.
wildcard.credentialsHint: Caddy only: one line per field of the DNS module, names as in its description (github.com/caddy-dns/<module>) — e.g. hetzner: auth_api_token=…, cloudflare: api_token=…, netcup: customer_number, api_key, api_password. Stored encrypted, never shown again. With Matcad they stay in Matcad.
edge.trustedIpsHint: The address the edge's requests arrive from at the hosts (public IP of the cloud server or its private-network address), comma-separated. Every Caddy host then trusts them, so the real visitor IP arrives.
picker.title: Choose instance
profiles.pluginNativeHint: This bundle holds compiled code. It cannot be edited here, only replaced (upload a new bundle) or downloaded. On an instance it runs only once the operator has switched on 'Allow native plugins' there — that cannot be set from here.
profiles.aiGuideAssistantPlaceholder: e.g. Always start pages with a hero and end with a call to get in touch. Address readers formally. Never delete pages.
aiprof.title: AI profiles
aiprof.help: Keep several connections – e.g. "DeepSeek Flash" and "OpenRouter free" – and activate one. The active one serves every AI call of every instance.
aiprof.name: Name
aiprof.nameHelp: Empty = made from provider and model.
aiprof.modelHelp: Type it or pick it after "Load models" – at OpenRouter also free models (…:free).
aiprof.activateConfirm: Activate "{0}"? Every instance uses it from its next AI call.
aiprof.chatgptIntro: This profile signs in to a ChatGPT account like the Codex app: show a code, enter it at OpenAI, done. Every ChatGPT profile has its own sign-in – two accounts are two profiles.
aiprof.saveFirst: Save the profile first – then sign in here with the ChatGPT account it should use.
profiles.aiGuideBotPlaceholder: e.g. Never name prices, always point to the contact form.
